_readme: Courtyard V2 — REPAINT THE GROUND IN PLACE (image-to-image).
RAHEEM'S IDEA, 2026-08-04: 'take the original image with the original castle, the
original lighting and all that, put it into Leonardo, jack the image-to-image
confidence up high, and just ask, can we change the castle floor to dirt... without
changing the castle or the angle. We could just swap them in and out.'
WHY THIS IS THE BETTER IDEA. Every earlier attempt generated a NEW floor and then
tried to make it agree with a castle it had never seen — which is why the angle, the
register and the palette each had to be fought separately. Image-to-image starts from
the finished plate, so the castle, the camera and the lighting are already correct by
construction and the only thing being asked for is the ground. It also sidesteps the
cut-out entirely: the output is a whole plate that drops in as a straight swap.
INIT IMAGE: src/assets/dev-preview/courtyard-v2-figma.png — the NEW courtyard being
designed on this branch. NOT public/assets/castle/courtyard.png: that is the shipped
production courtyard, and replacing ITS floor is pointless because the whole reason a
new floor is wanted is that we are moving off it. Raheem, 2026-08-04: 'Why would I be
trying to make a new courtyard if I was still using that one?' The new design lives in
dev-preview precisely because it is in progress and not in prod yet.
I got this wrong twice in one session, in opposite directions: first treating this
plate as the style authority for backgrounds, then dismissing it as a throwaway mock
and repainting the production courtyard instead. It is neither. It is the work in
progress, and it is the thing the new floor has to land in.
INIT STRENGTH IS THE WHOLE EXPERIMENT. In Leonardo, init_strength is how strongly the
result holds to the original, so HIGH preserves the castle and LOW lets the model
reinvent. Raheem wants it high. The ladder below brackets it — too high and the stone
paving survives untouched, too low and the towers start drifting. Read the results
before spending more: the useful value is the highest one that actually changed the
ground. Leonardo caps init_strength at 0.9.
NEGATIVE PROMPT IS DELIBERATELY SHORT. The usual anti-shadow and anti-perspective
bans are wrong here — we are KEEPING this plate's lighting and camera, not fighting
them. Banning shadow would ask the model to relight the castle, which is the opposite
of the brief. The day/night work goes back to being a separate job on a later pass.
COST: 4 generations, one per rung of the ladder.
